## Question

Can a simple physics model of a house's heat balance, plus a small neural network that
learns what the physics misses, predict indoor temperature better than either one alone,
and stay sensible in weather it has never seen?

## Approach

| Model | What it is | Why include it |
|---|---|---|
| Physics only | 1R1C ODE: `C dT/dt = (T_out - T_in)/R + Q_hvac + a·I_sol` | Interpretable baseline. R and C mean something physical. |
| ML only | MLP or LSTM on the same inputs | Black-box baseline |
| Hybrid | 1R1C + NN residual term, trained end to end in PyTorch | The point of the project |

## Plan: 2 weeks, Nov 17 to Dec 1, 2026

Assumes about 1 to 2 hours on weeknights and a longer block on weekends. Uses **synthetic
house data driven by real New York weather**, so nothing waits on a data request.
Thanksgiving is built in as a buffer.

### Week 1: data and baselines

| Day | Task | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Tue 11/17 – Wed 11/18 | **Setup in Positron.** Open the repo folder, create a virtual environment (`python -m venv .venv`), pick it as the interpreter, run `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Run `rc_model.py`, then `quarto preview` and open this page. (Optional: request ecobee Donate Your Data access, as a later extension.) | `rc_model.py` prints true vs fitted R, C |
| Thu 11/19 | **Real weather.** Download hourly NYC outdoor temperature and shortwave solar radiation for Jan to Feb 2025 from the free Open-Meteo historical API (no key needed). Save to `data/nyc_weather.csv`. | CSV with time, temp, solar |
| Fri 11/20 | **Synthetic house on real weather.** Change `synthetic_house()` to take the weather CSV. Make ~8 weeks of data. Split into train (mild weeks), validation, and test (the coldest week, as a "cold snap"). | Plot of indoor vs outdoor temp |
| Sat 11/21 | **Physics baseline.** Fit R, C, a_sol on train. Plot predicted vs actual on test. Table of fitted vs true parameters (shows the bias from hidden occupancy gains). | Figure 1 + table 1 |
| Sun 11/22 | **ML baseline.** Small MLP in PyTorch predicting next-step indoor temp from (T_in, T_out, Q_hvac, I_sol, hour of day). Evaluate a 24-hour rollout on test. | Test RMSE for ML-only |

### Week 2: hybrid model and write-up

| Day | Task | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Mon 11/23 | **Hybrid model, part 1.** PyTorch module: Euler step with learnable R, C, a_sol (initialised from Saturday's fit) plus a small NN residual term. | Model trains without errors |
| Tue 11/24 | **Hybrid model, part 2.** Train on 24-hour rollouts, add weight decay on the NN, tune lightly on validation. | Test RMSE for hybrid |
| Wed 11/25 | **Evaluation.** RMSE table for all 3 models on the cold-snap week. Recovered R and C vs true. Plot what the NN residual learned against the hidden occupancy signal. | Figures 2–4 + table 2 |
| Thu 11/26 – Fri 11/27 | **Thanksgiving buffer.** Catch up only if behind. | |
| Sat 11/28 | **Write-up, part 1.** Fill in Question, Approach, Results on this page. Code chunks pull from `rc_model.py`. | Page renders in `quarto preview` |
| Sun 11/29 | **Write-up, part 2.** Discussion: when the hybrid helps, limitations (synthetic data, 1R1C), next steps (ecobee data, 2R2C). | Full draft |
| Mon 11/30 | **Polish and publish.** Remove `draft: true`, run `quarto render`, delete the example project placeholders, commit `docs/` and `_freeze/`. | Live on GitHub Pages |
| Tue 12/1 | **Done.** Share the link (LinkedIn, resume). | |

### If you fall behind, cut in this order

1. Skip the ML-only baseline (compare physics vs hybrid only).
2. Skip the "what the NN learned" plot.
3. Use the sinusoidal weather already in `rc_model.py` instead of real weather.

### Later extensions (not in the 2 weeks)

- Repeat on real homes from the ecobee Donate Your Data set.
- 2R2C model (separate air and wall/mass temperatures).
